summary:
Adıyaman Province stands under the national framework of Türkiye. The provisions that govern a trans visitor's exposure in the province are national, and the source inventory contains no Adıyaman-specific carve-out from any of them: no local policing practice, no local facility rule and no local variation in the documents regime is documented for the province.

Same-sex sexual activity has been legal in Türkiye since 1858 under the Ottoman penal code, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, when gender reassignment surgery became legal. Türkiye has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and LGBTQ people are barred from serving openly in the military. Same-sex relationships receive no legal recognition: marriage, civil unions and domestic partnerships are unavailable, and same-sex couples cannot adopt jointly or as individuals.

A leaked draft omnibus justice reform, described by Human Rights Watch as the '11th Judicial Package', would enable criminal charges against LGBT people in Türkiye. Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that the draft would amount to one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades; Istanbul activists held a press conference against it on 28 October 2025. The package is national in scope and would apply countrywide if adopted, with no province-specific provisions; whether it has since passed is unresolved in the sources.
tangentialFactors:
The draft judicial package sits within a documented national pattern of escalating state hostility toward LGBT people: the Kaos GL LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 records 313 violations over the year, roughly two and a half times the 2024 total, dominated by 299 detention decisions. Turkish Minute's coverage of the same report counts six deaths linked to anti-LGBTQ violence in 2025, three classified as hate killings, with transgender individuals disproportionately affected.

Adıyaman Province has no documented record of its own on these measures. The province was struck by the February 2023 earthquakes, and any assessment of local institutional capacity should be read against that context, though the sources do not link it to LGBT-specific enforcement.
localsOnly:
Trans residents of Adıyaman Province change legal gender under the national procedure available since 1988, which requires gender reassignment surgery. No province-specific facility, employment or healthcare practice is documented.

Same-sex couples in the province cannot marry, enter a civil union or domestic partnership, or adopt jointly or individually, and no anti-discrimination law protects them on sexual orientation or gender identity. LGBTQ residents are barred from serving openly in the Turkish military.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted remains unresolved in the sources; the inventory records it as a leaked draft as of 29 October 2025.

No Adıyaman-specific policing data, detention records, hate-crime incidents or facility rules were identified in the inventory. The province-level picture is carried entirely by the national assessment.

The sources do not document how the national framework is applied in practice by Adıyaman's provincial authorities, courts or police.
